chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There are four things which will never be satiated by four other things: the Earth will never become satiated with rain; the eyes will never be satiated with seeing; women will never be satiated with men and scholars will never be satiated with knowledge.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things that never become satisfied according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to illustrate the natural inclination (*fitrah*) towards accumulation, contrasting the physical saturation of the earth with the spiritual and intellectual perpetuity of the scholar. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the endless pursuit of knowledge (*ilm*) as a defining characteristic of the learned, suggesting that true scholarship is a dynamic, unending journey rather than a static state of completion.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-47 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qad’dah that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq(MGB) said, “

There are four things which will never be satiated by four other things: the Earth will never become satiated with rain; the eyes will never be satiated with seeing; women will never be satiated with men and scholars will never be satiated with knowledge.”
